cross_method_lessons.lesson: A shared library endpoint does not imply a shared measurement mechanism.
examples: ClickSeq creates RNA-derived cDNA fragments; RASL ligates probe reporters; both yield DNA libraries.

cross_method_lessons.lesson: The useful shared unit is a scoped input-change-output relation, including what makes selection/copying/joining possible.
examples: cP-RNA needs original and post-treatment RNA end chemistry.
ClickSeq needs azido terminus and alkyne adapter partner.

cross_method_lessons.lesson: The same physical feature may be biological information, a reagent handle, or an artifact-control device depending on role.
examples: CAGE cap is an original RNA selection feature.
Biotin is a recovery handle across different selected objects.

cross_method_lessons.lesson: Chemical drawings have explicit roles; do not turn a legend molecule into an input or a reaction.
examples: AzNTP is a reagent structure; click-cycloaddition panel is an explicit transformation; biotin/psoralen figures are chemical references.

cross_method_lessons.lesson: A preparation can contain multiple chemical classes without branching the workflow.
examples: Bru-seq labelled and unlabelled RNA before enrichment

cross_method_lessons.lesson: Provenance survives even when the original chemical feature does not.
examples: Cap-selected cDNA is not capped DNA.
cP-selected DNA is not DNA carrying the original RNA cyclic phosphate.

minimal_graph_use.within_method: Represent source-described actions and preparation boundaries; attach specific reactive group, association, sequence/topology and selection-origin claims to the relevant participant. Preserve source grouping unless evidence requires a distinction.
cross_method_candidates: CAGE/TIF: compare use of capped RNA ends, but distinguish selection mechanism and single-end versus paired-end information.
RASL/ClickSeq: compare reporter-construction objectives while keeping probe ligation distinct from RNA copying and chemical adapter joining.
cP-RNA/Bru: compare selection logic, while distinguishing native end chemistry from introduced temporal label.
minimal_graph_use.historical_edges: No historical edge established by this review. Follow explicit cited primary development claims before recording built_on, adapted_from or a corresponding edge.
minimal_graph_use.chemical_encoding: Use supported reactive structures or identifiers at named constituents/groups when needed; symbolic RNA/DNA remainder is allowed. Whole mixed preparation need not have one formula/SMILES.
do_not_infer: Exact reaction conditions from a generic mechanism panel.
Physical separation from multiple molecule lines.
Same mechanism from shared action names or reagent shapes.
A chronological predecessor merely from a shared feature.
